entryAnswer.explanation:
Design: connectPushNumbers builds exactly one graph-registered source with the existing public factory fromPushNotification and returns {source, stop}.

1) Source creation. `graph.initNode(fromPushNotification<number>(register), [], { name: "pushNumbers" })` is the graph-bound operator/source funnel (packages/ts/src/graph/graph.ts:513-543, esp. 528-542); it delegates to the free initNode (packages/ts/src/graph/operators.ts:185-191, 204-222) and records the real factory name in the inspection index. fromPushNotification is a published source factory: packages/ts/src/graph/sources.ts:1210-1229, exported from @graphrefly/ts/sources (packages/ts/src/sources/index.ts:32) and the root (packages/ts/src/index.ts:373). It accepts PushRegister<T> = (deliver) => PushUnsubscribe | undefined (sources.ts:290-292) and returns Operator<never, T>, so the node is Node<number> and no deps are needed (a source is a depless operator; graph.ts:523-526).

2) When registration activates. The factory body runs ONCE on activation (sources.ts:4-9, 58-84): the source spec's setup is invoked by the node's activation path, and only then is `register(deliver)` called (sources.ts:1216-1221). Activation is subscriber-driven: Node.subscribe adds the sink, then calls _activate if not yet activated (packages/ts/src/node/node.ts:417-465, esp. 440-460). So `register` is not called at connectPushNumbers time; it runs when the first subscriber attaches — here our own forwarding subscription, or a caller subscription that happens first. Because register may deliver synchronously while registering, the factory's `deliver` closure is already installed and forwards via ctx.down([["DATA", payload]]) (sources.ts:1218-1220); those synchronous values are delivered as DATA waves and reach our sink, so 0 is forwarded like any other number. Protocol messages are filtered by the `msg[0] === "DATA"` guard: the closed message set includes START/DIRTY/RESOLVED/INVALIDATE/COMPLETE/ERROR/TEARDOWN/PAUSE/RESUME/PULL (packages/ts/src/protocol/messages.ts:21-32), and only DATA carries a value (messages.ts:24).

3) Cleanup semantics. The factory registers its teardown through ctx.onDeactivation (sources.ts:75-81): on deactivation it sets `done = true` (so late pushes are dropped) and calls the host's unsubscribe if register returned one (sources.ts:1222-1225). Deactivation happens when the node's subscriber set becomes empty: Node.subscribe's unsubscribe deletes the sink and calls _deactivate only when subscribers.size === 0 (node.ts:441-444), and nodeDeactivate runs the onDeactivation hooks (packages/ts/src/node/node-lifecycle-runtime.ts:76-83). Therefore: if another subscriber still remains (e.g. the caller later subscribed separately to `source`), our stop() removes only our sink, the subscriber set is non-empty, the node stays active, and the host registration cleanup is NOT run — the transport keeps delivering to the remaining subscriber. If ours was the last subscriber, the set becomes empty, the node deactivates, and the factory's cleanup runs: `done` flips and the host unsubscribe (when provided) is invoked, detaching the host listener.

4) Why stop is not a transport/Graph shutdown. stop() is idempotent (a `stopped` flag guards the single detach) and only calls the unsubscribe handle returned by our own subscribe (node.ts:417-419, 441-444). It detaches this function's own subscription; it does not call register, does not create another Graph, and does not open/close any connection. The factory's own contract says the host owns network/native setup and the factory owns reactive delivery and teardown only (sources.ts:1199-1204), and cleanup is best-effort deactivation, not a global shutdown. The caller-owned Graph and transport may have other subscribers, other nodes, or other registrations; stop cannot promise to shut them down, and the caller may later subscribe separately to `source` (which would re-activate it and re-run register).

5) Scope/authority. Only published entrypoints are used: @graphrefly/ts/sources for fromPushNotification and PushRegister, @graphrefly/ts/graph for Graph, @graphrefly/ts/core for Node. No source-relative imports, no invented modules, no direct register call, no extra Graph, no connection management. Caller callbacks are assumed not to throw. This is a static typecheck/source review; the snippet was not executed.
